name: LM3480IM3X-3.3_NOPB
title: 100 mA quasi low-dropout linear regulator in SOT-23, 3.3 V, 5 V, 12 V and 15 V
summary: LM3480 is a fixed-output linear regulator for loads up to 100 mA, made in 3.3 V, 5 V, 12 V and 15 V versions, in a three-pin SOT-23. It runs from inputs up to 30 V and needs at most 1.2 V of headroom at full load over temperature, against the 2 V to 2.5 V of the LM78Lxx family. Output tolerance is ±5 % over load and temperature. The 3.3 V version can be fed from a 5 V ±5 % rail.

notes: Stress past these limits may damage the part. Operation is guaranteed only within the recommended operating conditions, and the guaranteed limits are those of the electrical characteristics.

The allowed dissipation depends on ambient temperature: P = (TJ − TA) / RθJA. With TJ = 150 °C, TA = 50 °C and RθJA = 269.6 °C/W it is 370 mW; every degree of ambient below 50 °C adds 3.7 mW and every degree above takes 3.7 mW away. Heat sinking raises it. The part limits its own junction temperature at about 150 °C.

circuits.title: Typical application: 6.5 V in, 5 V at 100 mA out
circuits.description: The 5 V version fed from 6.5 V, giving 5 V at up to 100 mA. A 0.1 µF capacitor from IN to ground and another from OUT to ground are the only parts besides the regulator, the smallest values that keep it stable.

operation.text: A bandgap reference feeds an amplifier that drives a PNP and NPN pass stage between IN and OUT. Current-limit and thermal-shutdown blocks act on the drive. GND is the common return.

Four fixed outputs: 3.3 V, 5 V, 12 V and 15 V. The 5 V, 12 V and 15 V parts are offered as tiny SOT-23 alternatives to LM78Lxx-series regulators. With a 1.2 V worst-case dropout, the series fits applications where the 2 V to 2.5 V dropout of an LM78Lxx is too much.
The 3.3 V version works from 5 V ±5 %, so it can make a 3.3 V, 100 mA supply from a 5 V system rail.

Power dissipation is internally limited: the part holds its junction near 150 °C. Just after the output is shorted, about 255 mA flows from a 6.5 V input and about 370 mA from 20 V; the current then falls and later goes into thermal cycling.

Both input and output need at least 0.1 µF for stability and for acceptable transient response. No ESR window applies, though a very high ESR worsens the transient response. There is no upper limit on either capacitor; more output capacitance improves load-transient behaviour.
The input may be up to 30 V and should be well regulated. On a noisy input, extra low-ESR input capacitance helps the output noise.

The regulator, CIN and COUT sit on one side of the board, each capacitor next to its pin. The ground ends of CIN and COUT meet the GND pin over a wide copper area on the component side, with no vias or long traces in these connections. Short, wide connections keep parasitic inductance down, which reduces load-current transients and noise and aids stability. A ground plane, either inner or on the bottom layer under the part, holds output accuracy, screens noise and spreads heat; most designs need it to meet their thermal limits.
ESD protection on chip is limited; store and handle the parts with leads shorted or in conductive foam.
